II23A-01.note: Requires mapping compass corners to dredge (east) and heat (north) exposure; Cadfield (heat only) vs Aldmoss (heat+dredge) isolates dredging. C (Dellow>Cadfield) is tempting but supports Faulk; A is confounded by both factors; D is the reversal of a clean comparison.

II23A-02.note: Key pits logging-only Corlett against worms-only Ambersley on level ground, undercutting 'mainly earthworms'. The clean weakener (Ambersley not lighter than Fenwold) is absent and A is its supporting reversal; B is the slope trap; C weakens Elling, not Brevard.

II23A-03.note: Common-garden logic: city vs rural ordinary-weight seeds in the same garden. A (different gardens) is the most tempting; D uses the heavy-seed Esterholm confound; B points the wrong way.

II23A-04.note: Same pre-2010 year, burned-only Daleford beats fenced-only Carbery, so fences are not the main driver. C crosses the 2010 wet-summer boundary; B (fenced 2004 vs burned 1997) actually favors fences; D supports Cole but says nothing against fences directly.

II23A-05.note: Bramel (7 mites, no orchard) storing less than Ardane (3 mites, orchard) supports mites despite the pesticide working against it. D is the elevation trap (Cromby uplands, highest mites); B supports Dacosta; C contradicts Fenn.

II23A-06.note: Needs rats/area (Benvoray 6.2/ha) and chicks/nest (0.65) for each island. Ardvane (0.73 chicks/nest but only 4 rats/ha) is the strongest trap; Caillin and Dunvarra exceed 5 rats/ha but fall under 0.6.

II23A-07.note: The 0.4 m bolt offset puts the limit at 1.5 m on the table, so Cendry (1.3) is still below it; D (Cendry 38 vs Brockel 17) is the trap for students who read 1.1 off the table. A and C compare in the wrong direction or both above.

II23A-08.note: Copperhill drops 8 points and ripens in 66 < 71 days. Birchtop (A) ripens fastest and keeps the highest 35C value but drops 13 points, the main trap; options show only the 35C value so the drop must be computed from the table.

II23B-01.note: Leaky-only Ingold beats quarry-only Harrowfield on matched thick soil. The cleanest comparison (Ingold vs Jorvenn) appears only as the reversed A; B and C bring in Lammert's thin soil.

II23B-02.note: Meltwater-only Hamrin later than shade-only Isel. B isolates shade (supports Kalland) and is the most tempting since Kjelda has meltwater; C is confounded; D weakens Hovik.

II23B-03.note: Injection-only Gisler (2017) exceeds fracking-only Kvamby (2015), both after their onsets. A is confounded (Hollis has both); D brings in Jessenby's fault; C is a reversal that weakens.

II23B-04.note: Kvist (300 hikers, no horses) losing less than Gorrel (120, no horses, gentle) weakens the hiker dose claim. B weakens Hennum instead; D has Ingle's slope confound; A has horses.

II23B-05.note: POSSIBLE DEFECT: I find no clean weakener. The clean test (Gullhaven vs pre-irrigation Kelstad 2018) appears only as C, which supports Hagelin; A is explained away by Ljorn's clay, B by Kelstad's 2020 irrigation, D compares two inland wells. Picked B with low confidence.

II23B-06.note: Ivesk: 95 m and 18/8 = 2.25. Grinde clears 2 (2.14) but is 60 m; Hallum is deepest but 1.94; Jaren is deep but 1.67. Requires division plus a depth filter.

II23B-07.note: Iskilde fell 41 to 30, then rose 26.7%. Ludal (C) fell but rose only 15%, the main trap; Granberg (B) rose more than 20% but never fell; D's options give 2005 and 2020 only, so the 1990 column must be checked.

II23B-08.note: Only Jassel and Kolbeck have closest approach > 2.7. Jassel 3.4 vs Gyllen 1.6 is more than double; C (Kolbeck 6.3 vs Hennick 3.5) is 1.8x and the strongest trap; B uses Ivra, which counts as inside because its closest approach is 2.55 even though its farthest distance exceeds 2.7.

II23C-01.note: On the flat plain, stations-only Nettleford beats lanes-only Mossgate. B (Pellam vs Orrinby) is tempting but crosses the ridge/plain slope confound; D weakens Ruddock; C is confounded.

II23C-02.note: Weekdays, both rail towns with no bus lanes: Mellick charges and Pasterby does not. A is the trap (Norrance has no rail, plus weekday bus lanes); B reverses; C is confounded by rail.

II23C-03.note: Nethercote (porches, pre-rule) vs Quellin (no porches, pre-rule) holds cul-de-sacs fixed. The 'begun before/after' dating must be decoded; B is confounded (Morwen has both); D is the reversed form of the other clean pair; A supports Nakagawa.

II23C-04.note: Ruskett (nothing, near market) adopting before Merrigal (extension, near market) weakens Okoro. C is the distance trap (Nolby is far); A supports; D bears on Pemberton.

II23C-05.note: In 2017 Quorley had only the tax and Mistlow had nothing yet. D (Pendry before/after) is tempting but Pendry ran the campaign throughout and the region-wide decline confounds it; A supports Quarrie; C reverses.

II23C-06.note: County line is at +4 km, so Moxley (6) is just outside and Rindell (1) is inside and nearer the city. D and B run in the wrong direction; C compares two inside stations. A test-wise student can pick the only option with the farther station selling more.

II23C-07.note: Mavisford: 3.7 books per resident, 52 km. Ollerby (3.3, but 18 km) is the main trap; Pembray (2.94) is close on ratio; options omit the distance, so the table must be consulted.

II23C-08.note: Quillow: +$4.20 and 36/44 = 82%. Prestley (83% but +$3.90) is the strongest trap; Nanbury clears neither threshold cleanly; options give graduates and after-wage only, forcing two computations.

II23D-01.note: Sellwick sold less after its 1840 railway than before, with no market or school to confound it. A supports; B and D bring in market towns.

II23D-02.note: Upland Stavely (40 years, off road) beats upland Tessaby (none, on road). A (Vintrell 40 vs Wrayburn 15, both valley) is the strongest trap but is confounded by Vintrell's road; D crosses valley/upland; B bears on neither.

II23D-03.note: Both on the headland: company-only Sallowby loses less than ordinance-only Vexley. D (Skelby vs Vexley) is the harbor/headland trap; B and C contradict Ulvang.

II23D-04.note: In 1851, mill-rule-only Tenlow keeps children longer than board-only Sudmere. A crosses the 1858 slump; B supports Tennant; C weakens Vasquez. The clean weakener (Sudmere not later than Verrow) is absent; B is its supporting reversal.

II23D-05.note: Within Sarnby, clerks (eligible for plans) vs shopkeepers (not), with the conservatory equal for both. A is tempting but confounded by Sarnby's conservatory; C supports Szabo.

II23D-06.note: Stennard 9,800 to 21,500 (2.19x, 320 seats). Tavisholm more than doubles but has 610 seats; Ulvercote (1.87x) is close. Options show only 1900 attendance, so the comparison has to be made in the table.

II23D-07.note: Tarnside: 18.6 visitors per painting and 27.6% sold. Uxley sells 26% but draws 23 per painting; Yoxholt draws under 20 but sells 23.8%; Velmont fails both narrowly. Two ratios per option.

II23D-08.note: Vardleigh: 8 outlets for 9,400 = 1 per 1,175. Sedgeholm (1 per 1,040) is the trap because it had a grammar school; Wickerby, the largest, is 1 per 1,320.
